paragraphs: Friend, here's what this psalm is really about: who gets the credit, and who can carry you. It opens with "Not to us, O LORD, not to us, but to Your name be the glory" (Psalm 115:1), and it gives the reason: "because of Your loving devotion, because of Your faithfulness." Everything good that happens in your life traces back to that. So when something goes right, you get to hand the spotlight back and just say thank You.

Then the psalm sets two kinds of trust side by side. The idols are "silver and gold, made by the hands of men" (Psalm 115:4), and they have eyes that can't see and ears that can't hear. Meanwhile, "Our God is in heaven; He does as He pleases" (Psalm 115:3), and three times the psalm says of Him, "He is their help and shield" (Psalm 115:9-11). Whatever you lean on gets a say in who you become, because "Those who make them become like them, as do all who trust in them" (Psalm 115:8). So lean on the One who can actually hold you up, baker, and not on something that can't even clear its throat!

And look where the psalm lands. "The LORD is mindful of us; He will bless us" (Psalm 115:12), small and great alike, and that blessing reaches your children too (Psalm 115:13-14). The One who is "the Maker of heaven and earth" (Psalm 115:15) has not lost track of you. So the psalm ends the only way it can: "But it is we who will bless the LORD, both now and forevermore. Hallelujah!" (Psalm 115:18). While you've got breath, friend, praise Him.
